A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Llama-3.1 quantization study. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive rewriting and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy evaluations, GPTQ/AWQ comparisons, text-similarity measurements, and inference-performance experiments, with additional results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional RULER evaluations and latency-throughput analyses, alongside revised inference-performance results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same procedures: FP8 round-to-nearest quantization, INT8 GPTQ with dynamic activation quantization and SmoothQuant at 70B, and INT4 GPTQ with MSE-optimal clipping and 128-element groups. Calibration choices are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds RULER long-context evaluation on 8B and 70B models, extending coverage to retrieval, multi-hop tracing, information aggregation, and question answering with long inputs. Section 3.1 describes a 4k–128k sequence range; Table 3 explicitly excludes 405B because of computational cost. Existing accuracy benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: BF16 and the supported quantization formats, plus GPTQ versus AWQ in Table 1 and Appendix A.2. RULER extends existing format comparisons without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The reported vLLM version changes from 0.6.1.post2 to 0.6.4.post1. v1 reports latency-constrained asynchronous throughput for six workloads with explicit TTFT/ITL limits; v2 describes peak throughput and separately presents latency-throughput curves, omitting those numeric limits. Synchronous summarization is added, and the separate small-summarization case disappears. These changes prevent treating the performance tables as identical-setting comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 Figures 2–3 add two focused latency-throughput analyses: 8B docstring generation on one A6000 and 70B code fixing on two A100s. They examine where INT4's low-latency advantage gives way to INT8's throughput advantage. The existing text-similarity analysis is retained.

E5.justification: The two Arena-Hard runs, their averages, and 95% confidence intervals are unchanged between v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 6. Repeated-run reporting for GPTQ/AWQ is also retained. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds RULER scores, including 82.8 for 8B BF16 and 81.1 for INT4, and extensively replaces the inference-performance results. For example, the 8B/A6000 asynchronous speedup ranking changes from INT4 over INT8 (1.56 versus 1.16) to INT8 over INT4 (1.38 versus 1.08). These are results under revised protocols, not demonstrated same-setting performance changes. Existing appendix accuracy results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1 retains the same quantization definition, zero point, and scale. Neither version adds substantive theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations beyond the retained background.

C1.justification: The main accuracy conclusions remain. However, the abstract and introduction replace the earlier recommendation of INT4 for asynchronous deployment on mid-tier GPUs with broader emphasis on W8A8 maximizing asynchronous throughput. v2 also explicitly claims the first demonstration of GPTQ outperforming AWQ on real-world tasks.

C2.justification: v2 explains asynchronous format selection through the latency-throughput crossover, refining the earlier hardware-oriented recommendations. Its new Limitations section identifies untested embedding/head compression and multilingual applications; Table 3 also acknowledges the missing 405B long-context evaluation. Existing explanations of quantization and text similarity largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's benchmarking-data release statement and link, GuideLLM identification, detailed inference-backend discussion, and acknowledgements identifying LLM Compressor and LM Evaluation Harness. Core calibration and quantization details remain, and the vLLM version is updated. This changes the available reproducibility documentation without establishing that external resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 adds the RULER citation and removes the inference-framework subsection and associated citations, including Marlin and TensorRT-LLM, plus the introductory tweet references. The central positioning against earlier quantization evaluations remains, while GPTQ's advantage over AWQ receives an explicit first-demonstration claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, benchmark descriptions, and results discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. The inference-background subsection and acknowledgements are removed, a Limitations section is added, and the use-case table's retained settings move into prose. Affiliations and correspondence details also change.

P2.justification: v2 removes five accuracy bar charts and the use-case table, adds two latency-throughput plots, expands Table 3 with RULER, and restructures the performance tables. The text-similarity heatmaps, accuracy-recovery plot, and appendix pass@10 plots are retained and renumbered. Typography, first-page composition, and table placement change throughout.

improvement.justification: RULER evidence, latency-throughput curves, and concrete limitations improve coverage and interpretation. However, v2 removes the benchmarking-data link and introduces an apparent cost-reporting inconsistency: Table 5 reports 2.5 QPS and 187 queries/USD for BF16 405B on 16 A100s, whereas Table 8's pricing implies approximately 314 queries/USD. These opposing changes leave the net effect on the paper's central deployment guidance uncertain.
